dicas.texto: Você está indo muito bem! Lembre-se: se o denominador é 4, em quantas partes cada inteiro (de 0 a 1, de 1 a 2) foi dividido?
Ótimo! Agora, comece no zero e conte cada marcação de 1/4 até chegar em 6/4. Onde você para?
Quase lá! Como 4/4 é igual a 1, tente localizar o 1 na reta primeiro e conte mais duas marcações de 1/4 a partir dele.
Você está quase terminando! O ponto deve ficar exatamente na segunda marcação após o número 1. Tente clicar lá!

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 4 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: A fraction has a top number and a bottom number. Focus on the number above the fraction bar.
Read the fraction from top to bottom, then enter the top number in the upper box.
The upper number tells how many fourths are being considered.
Look directly above the fraction bar and type that numeral into the f1 field.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole.
Look below the fraction bar and enter the bottom number in the lower box.
The fraction is divided into fourths, so the denominator names the size of each part.
Read the numeral directly below the fraction bar and type it into the f2 field.
Compare the numerator and denominator to decide whether the fraction is greater than one whole.
When the numerator is larger than the denominator, use the conversion control to open the mixed-number fields.
The numerator contains more fourths than are needed for one whole.
After checking that the top number is larger, press the Convert button to reveal m1, m2, and m3.
A mixed number combines complete wholes with a remaining fraction of the same-sized parts.
Divide the numerator by the denominator: the quotient gives the whole number and the remainder gives the new numerator.
Use four fourths to make one whole, then determine how many fourths remain from the six fourths.
Enter the quotient in m1, the remainder in m2, and keep the denominator 4 in m3.
Use the denominator to identify the equal intervals in each whole on the number line.
Count fourths from zero, passing one whole after four fourths and continuing toward two.
After reaching one whole, count two more of the four equal intervals.
Place the point halfway between 1 and 2, at the location reached after six quarter-intervals.
Before finishing, check that the fraction and its position describe the same amount.
Review the numerator, denominator, mixed-number fields, and point on the number line.
Confirm that the point lies halfway between 1 and 2 and that the fraction fields show the given values.
When every field and the number-line mark has been checked, press the Done button.
